title: Licensing & the Road Test
summary: Riders under 18 must complete the Massachusetts Rider Education Program (MREP) basic rider course to get a motorcycle license.
By law a motorcycle has a seat or saddle and is built to run on no more than three wheels touching the ground.
Mopeds (motorized bicycles) are limited to 30 mph and 50 cc by design and may not be ridden faster than 25 mph; motorized scooters may not be ridden faster than 20 mph or between sunset and sunrise.

A limited use vehicle (top speed over 30 but not over 40 mph) needs a Class M license or permit if it is a motorcycle and may not use any road with a speed limit above 40 mph or limited-access highways.

You must be at least 16, apply, show valid ID, pay a fee, and pass a knowledge test to get a motorcycle learner's permit; applicants without a Class D license must also pass the Class D knowledge test.
Permit holders may ride only from sunrise to sunset and may never carry passengers.
You can apply for a Class M license at 16 and a half, and the permit converts to a license only after passing the road test or completing the MREP course.
Junior operators (under 18) must hold the permit six months with a clean record, take driver's education and the MREP course, and may not drive between 12:30 a.m. and 5:00 a.m.
Failing the motorcycle road test twice means you must complete an approved rider training course before scheduling another road test.
For the road test the motorcycle must be safe, registered, and inspected, and the rider must wear a DOT helmet meeting FMVSS No. 218 plus eye protection unless the bike has a windshield or screen.
Taking the road test on a trike or limited use vehicle earns a Class M license with a 'J' restriction limiting you to that type of vehicle.
The road test may include figure-eights and 360-degree circles in both directions without putting a foot down, along with starts, stops, turns, traffic, intersections, and hills.

questions.q: What is the minimum age to obtain a Massachusetts motorcycle learner's permit?
questions.explanation: An applicant for a motorcycle learner's permit must be at least 16 years old. Sixteen and a half is the minimum age to apply for the license itself.

questions.q: When is a motorcycle learner's permit holder allowed to ride?
options: Any time, if accompanied by a licensed rider
Only during daylight hours, from sunrise to sunset
Any time, but only on roads posted 40 mph or less
questions.explanation: Permit holders may operate a motorcycle only in daylight, from sunrise to sunset.

questions.q: May a motorcycle learner's permit holder carry a passenger?
options: No, passengers are prohibited for permit holders
Yes, if the passenger holds a Class M license
Yes, if the passenger is over 18
questions.explanation: Riders on a learner's permit are not allowed to carry any passengers.

questions.q: What happens if you fail the Class M road test twice?
options: You must wait one year before retesting
You must retake the knowledge test
You must complete an approved basic rider course before scheduling another road test
questions.explanation: After two failed motorcycle road tests, the RMV requires completion of an approved rider training course before another road test can be booked.

questions.q: A 17-year-old wants a Massachusetts motorcycle license. Which course must they complete?
options: The Massachusetts Rider Education Program basic rider course
No course is required if they pass the road test
questions.explanation: Anyone under 18 is required to successfully complete the MREP basic rider course to get a motorcycle license.

questions.q: How long must a minor hold a learner's permit before taking the road test for a Junior Operator's License?
questions.explanation: Junior operators must have held the learner's permit for at least six months, with a clean record over that period, before the road test.

questions.q: A rider under 18 may not operate a motor vehicle during which hours?
questions.explanation: Operators under 18 are barred from driving between 12:30 a.m. and 5:00 a.m.

questions.q: Under Massachusetts law, a motorcycle is designed to travel on how many wheels in contact with the ground?
options: Two, plus an optional sidecar wheel only if registered separately
questions.explanation: The legal definition covers motor vehicles with a seat or saddle built to run on no more than three wheels touching the ground.

questions.q: What is the maximum speed at which you may operate a moped (motorized bicycle) in Massachusetts?
questions.explanation: Moped riders must not exceed 25 mph, even though a moped can be built to reach up to 30 mph.

questions.q: Which rule applies to operating a motorized scooter in Massachusetts?
options: It may be ridden on limited-access highways in the right lane
It may carry one passenger with a helmet
It may not be ridden faster than 20 mph
It must be registered with the RMV
questions.explanation: Motorized scooters are capped at 20 mph; they also cannot carry passengers, use limited-access highways, or be registered by the RMV.

questions.q: On which roads is a limited use vehicle prohibited?
options: Any road with a speed limit above 40 mph
Any road with a speed limit above 30 mph
questions.explanation: Limited use vehicles may not be driven on limited-access or express highways or on any road posted above 40 mph.

questions.q: When is a motorcycle operator NOT required to wear eyeglasses, goggles, or a face shield?
options: When the motorcycle has a windshield or screen
questions.explanation: Eye protection is required unless the motorcycle is equipped with a windshield or screen.

questions.q: Massachusetts requires motorcycle helmets to comply with which standard?
options: Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 108
Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standard No. 218
Any helmet sold by a licensed dealer
questions.explanation: Helmets must meet the US DOT's FMVSS No. 218 and carry stickers showing compliance inside and out.

questions.q: During the Class M road test, how must you perform figure-eights and 360-degree circles?
options: In both directions without your feet touching the roadway
In one direction only, with one foot down allowed
At a minimum speed of 15 mph
questions.explanation: The examiner may ask for figure-eights and full circles in both directions, completed without putting your feet down.

questions.q: To avoid being charged the road test fee, at least how far in advance must you cancel or reschedule your road test?
questions.explanation: Cancelling or rescheduling less than 72 hours before the test time results in the road test fee being charged.
